T-Systems (T Cloud Public).summary_note: T Cloud Public (formerly Open Telekom Cloud) is Germany's flagship sovereign public cloud and holds the most comprehensive EU certification portfolio of any European public cloud provider — BSI C5:2020 Type 2, ISO 27001/17/18, SOC 1/2/3, TISAX, and IT-Grundschutz registration. Deutsche Telekom's KRITIS designation, ~32% German state ownership (via KfW), and GAIA-X founding membership place it at the apex of EU strategic sovereignty. However, the platform's most significant and persistent sovereignty weakness is its co-development with Huawei Technologies (Chinese) using Huawei FusionSphere as the core cloud OS since 2016. China's National Intelligence Law (2017) theoretically obliges Huawei to cooperate with Chinese state intelligence, and Huawei hardware supplies server infrastructure to this day (though T-Systems is diversifying vendors). T-Systems asserts Huawei has zero operational access during production, and the platform is OpenStack-certified allowing independent operation, but the FusionSphere software origin is an unresolved supply-chain sovereignty concern (SOV-2, SOV-5). Deutsche Telekom's newer Industrial AI Cloud deliberately excludes both Huawei and US hyperscalers, signalling awareness of this gap. For EU workloads requiring the highest jurisdictional assurance, T Cloud Public scores highly on legal, operational, and environmental sovereignty — but the Huawei supply-chain heritage prevents a clean sweep on supply-chain (SOV-5) and legal/extraterritorial (SOV-2) dimensions.
